details.label: Medium

suggested_questions: Why is there so much gold?

knowledge_base.title: Belvedere: The Kiss
knowledge_base.content: The Kiss was painted by Gustav Klimt in 1907–08, during his Golden Phase. It shows a couple in an intimate embrace against a gold ground. Klimt used oil paint with gold and silver leaf on canvas. The square work measures 180 by 180 centimetres and is in the collection of the Belvedere in Vienna.

knowledge_base.title: Looking closely at The Kiss
knowledge_base.content: The man wears a robe with black-and-white rectangular motifs, while the woman's dress has colourful circular and floral forms. The couple stand at the edge of a flower-filled meadow. Their faces and hands are rendered more naturalistically than the highly patterned clothing and gold background. The gold ground flattens space and makes the figures feel both intimate and icon-like.
